units.title: The parking-lot incident
units.preview: The narrator introduces a collision and asks how responsibility could be assigned.
units.question: What two different accounts of the collision do you hear?

units.title: Campus protests and the official response
units.preview: Students’ questions, the president’s account, and disciplinary consequences are compared.
units.question: Which details are attributed to an official statement, and which are the narrator’s interpretation?

units.title: Introducing the lawsuit and reporting limits
units.preview: The narrator switches to the civil case, describes the dispute, and explains why the accusations cannot be treated as legal findings.
units.question: What language does the host use to distinguish accusations from established findings?

units.title: Fraternities and insurance risk
units.preview: Background on fraternities, liability, exclusions, and how members may lose coverage.
units.question: Why do insurance exclusions matter in this background section?

units.title: Risk, lawsuits and campus incentives
units.preview: A discussion of common claims, risky initiation practices and why institutions keep fraternity housing.
units.question: What financial or institutional reasons does the host discuss?

units.title: A former member’s account
units.preview: The narrator discusses a former fraternity member’s allegations about initiation and the chapter house.
units.question: Whose personal account is described, and how is it related to the larger story?

units.title: Events before the alleged incident
units.preview: The story turns to a drug-related arrest, campus oversight, and the timeline leading into the lawsuit.
units.question: How does the narrator connect the earlier incident to the upcoming allegations?

units.title: The timeline presented in the lawsuit
units.preview: The narrator traces locations and people while reporting disputed claims from the court filing.
units.question: Can you reconstruct the locations in chronological order while keeping claims attributed?

units.title: Messages and competing interpretations
units.preview: The host reviews group-chat material and stresses the difference between what messages show and what someone infers.
units.question: Which statements are directly reported, and which are interpretations of the messages?

units.title: An additional lawsuit and later reporting
units.preview: A separate filing, partial investigation records, and later reported developments complicate the narrative.
units.question: Why might different filings describe overlapping events differently?

units.title: Investigations, outcomes and the close
units.preview: The episode recounts institutional procedures, disciplinary outcomes, and the later public lawsuit.
units.question: How do university discipline and criminal prosecution differ in this account?
